_note: Goes into public.clients.theme for slug 'bouldering-project'. Every value except the four marked DERIVED was measured off boulderingproject.com on 2026-08-24. Changing any of these is a config update — no code change, no redeploy.

measured.#3D3935: dominant page background AND dominant text color — 2,644,331px² of background coverage. Their signature warm dark.
measured.#97A2BA: secondary surface, 142,000px². Cool blue-grey. Used here as muted text and as the 'settled' state color.
measured.#D65F52: the real accent. Low area (11,737px²) but present across background, text, AND border — the signature of an emphasis color, not a surface. The extractor's frequency heuristic mislabeled #97A2BA as the accent; this is the correction.
measured.#4E5569: measured but NOT used — a third cool grey that muddies the palette against the warm ground. Dropped deliberately.
measured.#FFFFFF: text and borders on the dark ground.

derived.surface: #4A4540 — a lift off #3D3935. Their site has no card surface to measure because it isn't a dashboard.
derived.sunk: #332F2C — a recess below the ground, same reason.
derived.line: White at 13%. Their hairlines are solid white, which is too loud at dashboard density.
derived.accentSoft: The accent at 14%, for active navigation.

substitutions.typeface: Their site runs FF Good Pro across every role, self-hosted with no Google Fonts link. It is a licensed webfont — serving it from our domain would breach the license and likely fail referrer checks. Archivo is the substitute: a grotesque built for condensed uppercase display work and the closest free match to Good Pro's character. 'Good Pro' stays first in the stack so it renders correctly the moment a licensed kit is installed.
substitutions.case: Their site sets text-transform:uppercase on h1, h2, AND body. Adopted for labels, navigation, eyebrows, and state chips — dropped for body copy. Uppercase running text at dashboard density is hard to read, and their CEO reads this weekly.
substitutions.logo: Left null on purpose. Their logo files (logo--black.svg, logo-footer.svg) live on their WordPress server; hotlinking is fragile, and the black variant is invisible on the dark ground. Until they send an asset we host ourselves, the wordmark renders as type — which matches their brand, since their logo IS a wordmark.
